# Legacy observations: V3 previous / next file order (local probe, 2026-10-13)

Captured by the `legacy_next_file_capture` probe ([`next_file_capture.cpp`](../../../../tools/legacy-capture/next_file/next_file_capture.cpp), its own project in [`tools/legacy-capture/next_file/`](../../../../tools/legacy-capture/next_file/CMakeLists.txt)) on the folder [`inputs/next-file-names.txt`](../../../../tools/legacy-capture/inputs/next-file-names.txt) describes. [`extract_functions.py`](../../../../tools/legacy-capture/extract_functions.py) copies `VideoBox::NextFile` (`HikariSub/VideoBox.cpp:682-739` at `20d647c4`) out of its file unchanged; it is compiled against a static wxbase built from the legacy checkout's own `Thirdparty/wxWidgets` submodule (v3.3.3, `670835ae`), so `wxDir::GetAllFiles(pathwn, &files, emptyString, wxDIR_FILES)` is the pinned wx's `src/unix/dir.cpp`. The GUI NextFile calls is stood in for by [`next_file/standins.h`](../../../../tools/legacy-capture/next_file/standins.h): every file opens (`OpenFile` returns true and sets the tab's `VideoPath`), and `Seek`, `Pause` and `SetFocus` are recorded.

Each file is one JSON object: the platform, wx's version, the folder's file system, the entries as created (in the names file's order, which is deliberately not a sorted one), the folder as the system enumerates it (`readdir`, every entry), NextFile's listing (its `files` member, also checked equal to a direct `wxDir::GetAllFiles` call) and two walks: VIDEO_NEXT_FILE pressed from the listing's first video until NextFile seeks instead of opening, and VIDEO_PREVIOUS_FILE from its last video.

`windows.json` comes from the winix task `legacy-win-next-file` ([`windows/next-file.ps1`](../../../../tools/legacy-capture/windows/next-file.ps1)), which builds the same probe with MSVC in the VM against the same wx pin (wxDir's `src/msw/dir.cpp`, `FindFirstFileW`).

## What legacy does

Legacy's order is the file system's own, unsorted. In all three captures the listing is exactly the enumeration with the folder (`folder.mkv`) and the `.` name (`.dotted.mkv`) left out, and each walk is the listing's videos after (before) the start in that order, then `seek 0`, `pause false`. The order itself differs between file systems for the same names created in the same order: btrfs and xfs (a small folder) enumerate in creation order, tmpfs in the reverse of it; ext4 (not captured here) enumerates a hashed folder in the order of its name hashes, which depend on the file system's seed. No name order (byte, case-insensitive, natural, locale) is involved on Linux. On Windows (`windows.json`) wx's `FindFirstFileW` on NTFS returns the names in the volume's index order, upper-cased UTF-16 code units (`.dotted.mkv`, `a.b.mkv`, `a.mkv`, `B.mkv`, `c.MKV`, `ep1.mkv`, `ep10.mkv`, `ep2.mkv`, ..., `_under.mp4`, `~tilde.avi`, `Ärger.mkv`, `é.mkv`, `日本語.mkv`), whatever the creation order; the listing also leaves out the file with the hidden attribute (`attr-hidden.mkv`: wxDir without `wxDIR_HIDDEN`) and, unlike Linux, keeps `.dotted.mkv` (a leading dot hides nothing on Windows).

## Compared with the rewrite

These captures record legacy at the baseline (`20d647c4`). On 2026-10-14 the User chose natural name order for the previous / next file in both apps instead of the file system's order (`V3-next-file-natural-order` in [compatibility-decisions.md](../../../../docs/qt/compatibility-decisions.md); legacy main sorts the same way in `HikariSub/NaturalOrder.cpp`), so the walks here are no longer the rewrite's.

`ShellTests::nextFileWalksTheCaptureFolderInNaturalOrder` (`hikari_ui_shell_tests`) reads the observation for the platform it runs on (it skips, naming the file, when that platform's is absent): it checks the relation above in the observation (listing = enumeration filtered, unsorted; the walks follow the listing), which is still how the rewrite lists the folder. It makes the same folder in the same order (the videos are copies of the `cfr.mkv` media fixture so each one opens) and walks it with `Application::nextVideoFile` both ways, which must open the listing's videos in natural name order (case left out, digit runs as numbers: `_under.mp4`, `a.b.mkv`, `a.mkv`, `attr-hidden.mkv` on Linux, `B.mkv`, `c.MKV`, `ep1.mkv`, `ep2.mkv`, `ep10.mkv`, `~tilde.avi`, `Ärger.mkv`, `é.mkv`, `日本語.mkv`), whatever this file system's enumeration order is. On Windows with both folders on NTFS the enumeration must also equal the observed one, since NTFS's order does not depend on the creation order.
